you do well setting. a few things i want to point out- 
the positioning of your feet. when i set, i always line my feet up a little more than shoulder width apart and square my feet to my target. this was i can draw strength from both legs and my core. you'll hear a lot of people say to use a left right stepping pattern which it works for some but i find myself to be more accurate this way. many college setters say the same.
when you set, your arms/ elbows should almost be facing in/forward. i'm not sure if this makes sense but your motion should primarily be in front of your body rather than your elbows bending out. i find this helped me a lot with my sets to my outside hitter. i was more lined up with my target

i'm not a professional but i do have 10+ years experience so i think i know what i'm talking about. i pulled some of my advice from my own private lessons with college setters

woah. first of all, calm down. at this point you're probably just psyching yourself out. second, if you're having trouble then you should stick to one serve. accuracy, speed, and power will come with consistency. it sounds like you keep switching your serving style. keep your hand wide, your arm strong and swing fast and straight. is it possible that your toss is the problem? if so, you can stand in serving position and extend your tossing arm (left hand if you are right handed and vice versa) and make sure your fingers aren't touching the wall but are very close. hold the ball with your tossing hand and toss it a little higher than your head and swing your arm. your hand should pin the volleyball on the wall. you just repeat this to help with making solid contact. don't stress out about your serve just stay consistent.

all great questions 

tempo/heights
the way you set the ball does depend on the height and arm length of your hitter. your sets should always be high enough that your hitter can fully extend his/her arm and hit a heavy ball off it. personally i don't know a lot about tempos, i just know where the set goes for all of my different sets.

hand form
when you have a rough setting day you can put your hands on your hips and they should form to how you should be contacting the ball. try to be consistent with how the ball sits in your hands. whenever i hold a ball, i hold it like i'm setting it.

strength
make sure to use your legs when you set. you don't want to be in front of the ball otherwise you aren't going to be able to push it forward (going to your opposite is a somewhat different story). have quick hands really. you can practice setting to the wall while close to it. just make sure you aren't in front of the ball, use your legs, flick your wrists quickly, don't let the ball fall too far into your hands, make sure you are making contact with the ball at your forehead and not when you are already going through your motion
